question: A boat can travel 21 km in 3 hours going upstream. It can travel 55 km in 5 hours going downstream. What is the speed of the stream?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream Speed (D) = 55 ÷ 5 = 11 km/h

Upstream Speed (U) = 21 ÷ 3 = 7 km/h

Speed of Stream = (D − U) ÷ 2 = (11 − 7) ÷ 2 = 2 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Upstream Distance = 21 km, Time = 3 h; Downstream Distance = 55 km, Time = 5 h.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Speed of stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

 U = 21/3 = 7 km/h
 D = 55/5 = 11 km/h
 Stream Speed (y) = (D − U) / 2
 
 
 

 
 

⇒ Downstream speed (D) = 55 ÷ 5 = 11 km/h

⇒ Upstream speed (U) = 21 ÷ 3 = 7 km/h

⇒ Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed of stream = (11 − 7) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed of stream = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

It is calculated as the average of the downstream and upstream speeds: Speed = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Downstream and Upstream Relation

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream. Upstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water − Speed of stream.

Relative Speed in Water

When moving with the flow, the speeds add up; when moving against the flow, the stream speed is subtracted from the boat speed.</p
